name: Niamh
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Niamh is a great fairy queen of Ireland. Her names are several, among them Neeve, Niave, Niam, Niau, and Niamh of the Golden Hair. Her beauty was such that no man could turn away, and the name itself means beauty. She was the child of Manannán Mac Lir, lord of the ocean, and made her home far out at sea, on the enchanted isle of Tir Tairngiri, the land of promise. She took her captive lovers there. Her most famous lover was Oisín, a bard of the Fianna. He left his comrades to follow her to her Otherworld, where they had a daughter named Plur na mBan, which means flower of womanhood. Oisín grew homesick and begged to return to Ireland. Niamh warned him that his foot must not touch the ground. She set him astride a fairy steed and let him ride home. In Ireland he found the Fianna long gone and the old gods vanished. He fell from the horse and died of old age. Two other women also bear the name Niamh. One was the mistress of the hero Cúchulainn. The second one was wed to a prince of the court of Concobar Mac Nessa.
